source.text: Τότε οὖν ἔλαβεν ὁ Πιλᾶτος τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἐμαστίγωσεν.

records.literal_gloss: Then therefore took the Pilate the Jesus and flogged [him].

en.L: Then Pilate therefore took Jesus and flogged [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}].
en.B: Then Pilate took Jesus and had {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} flogged.
en.R: So Pilate took Jesus and had {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} whipped.

vi.L: Bấy giờ Phi-lát bắt Đức Giê-xu và đánh roi [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}].
vi.B: Rồi Phi-lát bắt Đức Giê-xu và cho lính đánh roi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Vậy Phi-lát bắt Đức Giê-xu và cho người lấy roi đánh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그때 빌라도가 예수를 데려다가 채찍질하였다.
ko.B: 그때 빌라도는 예수를 데려다가 채찍질하게 했다.
ko.R: 그래서 빌라도는 예수를 끌고 가서 채찍으로 때리게 했다.

decisions.choice: Pilate took Jesus and flogged him: Pilate ordered it and his soldiers carried it out
alternatives: Pilate flogged Jesus with his own hands
decisions.reason: A governor did not wield the whip himself. Greek, like many languages, says that a person did what he had others do; the soldiers who go on to mock Jesus (verses 2-3) are the ones who carried out the order. The responsibility is Pilate's.

decisions.choice: flogged: beaten with a whip, a Roman punishment
alternatives: the flogging that was part of the sentence of crucifixion
decisions.reason: The verb means to whip or scourge. Roman flogging was a severe beating that could be given as a punishment on its own or before a crucifixion (Mark 15:15). In John it comes before any sentence is passed, and afterward Pilate brings Jesus out and says again that he finds no case against him (verses 4-6). It seems Pilate hoped the beating would be enough for Jesus's accusers, as Luke 23:16, 22 says he proposed ("I will punish him and release him"). John tells it in a single word and gives no details.

decisions.choice: then therefore: after the choice of Barabbas
decisions.reason: The two linking words tie this to 18:39-40: Pilate offered to release Jesus for the feast, and they shouted for Barabbas instead. So Pilate turns to another way of dealing with the case.

decisions.choice: had him flogged (B); had him whipped (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "had" so that no reader pictures the governor wielding the whip himself (meaning decision m1). Readable uses the everyday word "whipped".

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrator uses "예수께서", "그분" and the honorific -시- for Jesus
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide, section 7). Recorded once for this passage.

source.text: καὶ οἱ στρατιῶται πλέξαντες στέφανον ἐξ ἀκανθῶν ἐπέθηκαν αὐτοῦ τῇ κεφαλῇ, καὶ ἱμάτιον πορφυροῦν περιέβαλον αὐτόν, καὶ ἤρχοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ ἔλεγον· Χαῖρε, ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων· καὶ ἐδίδοσαν αὐτῷ ῥαπίσματα.

records.literal_gloss: And the soldiers, having woven a crown out of thorns, put [it] on of him the head, and a robe purple they threw around him, \v 3 and they were coming to him and were saying, "Hail, the king of the Jews!" and they were giving him blows.

en.L: And the soldiers, having woven a crown out of thorns, put [it] on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head, and they threw a purple robe around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \v 3 and they kept coming up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and saying, "Hail, King of the Jews!" and they kept giving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} blows.
en.B: The soldiers wove a crown out of thorns and set it on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head, and they dressed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in a purple robe. \v 3 Again and again they came up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Hail, King of the Jews!" and struck {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the face.
en.R: The soldiers twisted some thorny branches into a crown and put it on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head. They put a purple robe on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 3 They kept coming up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and saying, "Long live the King of the Jews!" And they kept hitting {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the face.

vi.L: Các binh lính bện một vương miện bằng gai, đặt lên đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và khoác cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một áo choàng màu tía, \v 3 rồi họ cứ đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nói: "Kính chào, Vua của người Do Thái!" và cứ tát {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Lính bện một vương miện bằng gai, đội lên đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và mặc cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một áo choàng màu tía. \v 3 Họ cứ lần lượt đến trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nói: "Kính chào Vua dân Do Thái!" rồi tát vào mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Những người lính lấy cành gai bện thành một vương miện và đội lên đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ khoác cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một áo choàng màu tía. \v 3 Họ cứ đến trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nói: "Vua dân Do Thái vạn tuế!" Rồi họ cứ tát vào mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 병사들은 가시로 관을 엮어 그분의 머리에 씌웠고, 자주색 옷을 그분께 둘러 입혔다. \v 3 그리고 그분께 계속 다가와서 "유대인의 왕, 만세!" 하고 말하며, 계속 손바닥으로 그분을 때렸다.
ko.B: 병사들은 가시나무로 관을 엮어 예수의 머리에 씌우고, 자주색 옷을 입혔다. \v 3 그리고 잇달아 예수 앞으로 나와서 "유대인의 왕, 만세!" 하고 외치며 손바닥으로 그분의 얼굴을 때렸다.
ko.R: 병사들은 가시 돋친 가지를 엮어서 왕관을 만들어 예수의 머리에 씌웠다. 그리고 자주색 옷을 입혔다. \v 3 병사들은 자꾸 예수 앞으로 다가와서 "유대인의 왕 만세!" 하고 외쳤다. 그리고 예수의 얼굴을 계속 때렸다.

decisions.choice: a crown of thorns and a purple robe: the dress of a mock king
alternatives: a crown meant chiefly to cause pain
decisions.reason: The word for crown means a wreath or garland, such as rulers and victors wore. Purple dye was costly, and purple clothing marked royalty and high office (Judges 8:26; 1 Maccabees 10:20). The soldiers dress Jesus up as a king to make fun of the charge that he claimed to be one (18:33-37). The thorns would have hurt, but what John shows is the mockery. Mark 15:17 also says purple; Matthew 27:28 calls the robe scarlet.

decisions.choice: Hail: the greeting with which a ruler was acclaimed, here given in mockery
decisions.reason: The word was an everyday greeting, but it was also the cry with which subjects hailed a king or the emperor. The soldiers come up one after another and pay mock homage, as if to a ruler (Matthew 27:29; Mark 15:18). The form with the article ("the king") is used here as a form of address.

decisions.choice: the King of the Jews: a royal title for the king of the Jewish nation
decisions.reason: This is the title Pilate has used (18:33, 39), the claim the soldiers mock. "The Jews" here means the Jewish people as a nation, as in any royal title; the soldiers, who are Roman, mock both Jesus and the people whose king he is said to be. It does not mean the authorities. Pilate will set the same title over the cross (19:19).

decisions.choice: blows: blows with the hand, given again and again
decisions.reason: The noun means a blow, usually a slap with the open hand, though it can be a blow with a rod; it is the word used when an officer struck Jesus before Annas (18:22). The verbs "were coming", "were saying" and "were giving" are all imperfect: the soldiers did this repeatedly.

decisions.choice: Long live (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the cry that young readers know for greeting a king. Literal and Balanced keep "Hail", the usual word for acclaiming a ruler (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: struck him in the face (B); kept hitting him in the face (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the blows fell, since the word usually means slaps to the face (meaning decision m4). Balanced shows the repetition with "again and again", Readable with "kept".

decisions.choice: "vương miện bằng gai"
decisions.reason: "mão" is the older word; "vương miện" is today's plain word for a king's crown, and the mockery is of a king.

decisions.choice: "vạn tuế" (R); "Kính chào" (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Vua ... vạn tuế!" is how Vietnamese acclaims a ruler, so Readable makes the mock acclamation plain, as the English "Long live" does.

decisions.choice: "만세" for the greeting chaire at every level
decisions.reason: The word is the acclamation given to a ruler (meaning decision); "만세" is the Korean acclamation of a king, here in mockery. A greeting such as "평안하라" would lose the royal sense.

source.text: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν πάλιν ἔξω ὁ Πιλᾶτος καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἴδε ἄγω ὑμῖν αὐτὸν ἔξω, ἵνα γνῶτε ὅτι οὐδεμίαν αἰτίαν εὑρίσκω ἐν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And went out again outside the Pilate and says to them, "See, I bring to you him outside, that you may know that no case I find in him."

en.L: And Pilate went outside again and says to them, "See, I am bringing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out to you, so that you may know that I find no case in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: Pilate went outside again and said to them, "Look, I am bringing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out to you, so that you may know that I find no case against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: Pilate went outside again. He said to the people there, "Listen! I am bringing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out to you. I want you to know that I find no reason to condemn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

vi.L: Phi-lát lại đi ra ngoài và nói với họ: "Này, tôi dẫn người này ra cho các ông, để các ông biết rằng tôi không tìm thấy một cớ nào nơi người này."
vi.B: Phi-lát lại ra ngoài và nói với họ: "Này, tôi đưa người này ra cho các ông, để các ông biết rằng tôi không tìm thấy cớ nào để buộc tội ông ta."
vi.R: Phi-lát lại ra ngoài. Ông nói với những người ở đó: "Hãy nghe đây! Tôi đưa ông ta ra cho các ông. Tôi muốn các ông biết rằng tôi không tìm thấy lý do gì để kết án ông ta."

ko.L: 그리고 빌라도가 다시 밖으로 나가서 그들에게 말한다. "보아라, 내가 그에게서 아무 죄목도 찾지 못한다는 것을 너희가 알게 하려고, 그를 너희에게 밖으로 데리고 나온다."
ko.B: 빌라도가 다시 밖으로 나가서 그들에게 말했다. "보아라, 내가 그를 너희 앞으로 데리고 나오겠다. 내가 그에게서 아무 죄도 찾지 못하겠다는 것을 너희가 알게 하려는 것이다."
ko.R: 빌라도가 다시 밖으로 나갔다. 그리고 거기 있는 사람들에게 말했다. "들어라! 내가 그를 너희 앞으로 데리고 나오겠다. 나는 이 사람을 처벌할 이유를 하나도 찾지 못하겠다. 너희가 그것을 알기를 바란다."

decisions.choice: case: grounds for a charge, a legal reason to punish
decisions.reason: The word means the cause or ground of an accusation, the basis on which a court condemns someone. It is not a word for moral fault. Pilate says this three times (18:38; 19:4, 6): Roman justice, in his own judgment, has nothing against Jesus.

decisions.choice: I am bringing him out so that you may know: the beaten man is shown as proof that Pilate has found nothing
alternatives: Pilate hoped they would pity him
decisions.reason: John does not explain how bringing Jesus out shows this. It seems Pilate meant the sight of the flogged prisoner in mock dress to show that the charge was empty and that he had been punished enough. Yet the governor who says he finds no case has just had him flogged.

decisions.choice: them: those outside the praetorium who brought the charge
decisions.reason: Pilate has gone out to them before (18:29, 38). They are the chief priests and their officers (19:6), with those who stood with them outside; John calls them "the Jews" in 18:38. They stayed outside so as not to become unclean before the Passover (18:28).

decisions.choice: says (Literal); said (Balanced, Readable); likewise in verses 5, 6, 9, 10, 14 and 15
decisions.reason: John often tells a story in the present tense ("he says") for vividness. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told in this language. This applies to every such verb in the passage.

decisions.choice: I find no case in him (Literal); I find no case against him (Balanced); I find no reason to condemn him (Readable); the same at 18:38 and 19:6
alternatives: I find no fault in him
I find no guilt in him
decisions.reason: "Case" carries the legal sense of the word (meaning decision m1); Readable says plainly what having no case means. Each level uses the same English each time Pilate says it, so the reader hears the repetition. Readable adds "to the people there" and "I want you to know" to make the short sentences clear.

decisions.choice: "nói" with no past marker (L); past shown by context (B, R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has no tense ending, so Literal keeps John's historic present by leaving out "đã" here and in verses 5, 6, 9, 10, 14 and 15; Balanced and Readable read as past narrative.

decisions.choice: "người này", "ông ta" in Pilate's mouth, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Pilate and the accusers speak of Jesus as "người này" or "ông ta" and to him as "anh". These are their words, not the narrator's deity pronoun, so they are not capitalised where the English has a span. The narrator keeps "Ngài" with the span. Kept through this passage.

decisions.choice: historic present "말한다" (L); past (B, R), here and in verses 5, 6, 9, 10, 14 and 15
decisions.reason: Literal keeps John's present tense in narrative; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past. One decision for 19:1-16.

source.text: ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἔξω, φορῶν τὸν ἀκάνθινον στέφανον καὶ τὸ πορφυροῦν ἱμάτιον.

records.literal_gloss: Went out therefore the Jesus outside, wearing the thorny crown and the purple robe.

en.L: So Jesus went outside, wearing the thorny crown and the purple robe.
en.B: So Jesus came outside, still wearing the thorny crown and the purple robe.
en.R: So Jesus came out. He was wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe.

vi.L: Vậy Đức Giê-xu đi ra ngoài, đội vương miện gai và mặc áo choàng màu tía.
vi.B: Vậy Đức Giê-xu bước ra ngoài, vẫn đội vương miện gai và mặc áo choàng màu tía.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu bước ra. Ngài đội vương miện gai và mặc áo choàng màu tía.

ko.L: 그래서 예수께서 가시관을 쓰시고 자주색 옷을 입으신 채 밖으로 나가셨다.
ko.B: 그래서 예수께서 가시관을 쓰고 자주색 옷을 입으신 채로 밖으로 나오셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 밖으로 나오셨다. 예수께서는 가시관을 쓰고 자주색 옷을 입고 계셨다.

decisions.choice: wearing: still dressed as the soldiers had dressed him
decisions.reason: The present participle describes what he had on as he came out: the mock crown and robe of verse 2. Jesus is presented to his accusers in the costume of the mockery.

decisions.choice: the crown and the robe: mockery of a king, which John's reader knows is in fact a king
decisions.reason: Jesus has told Pilate that he is a king, though his kingdom is not from this world (18:36-37). The soldiers mean the crown and robe as a joke; the Gospel's reader sees the true king dressed up as a false one. John lets the scene speak and does not comment.

decisions.choice: went out: out of the praetorium to where his accusers waited
decisions.reason: The same verb and the same word "outside" were used of Pilate in verse 4. Jesus comes out of the governor's headquarters into the open place where the chief priests stood (18:28).

decisions.choice: came out (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable tell it from the point of view of those waiting outside, as verse 4 has prepared. Literal keeps "went".

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἰδοὺ ὁ ἄνθρωπος.

records.literal_gloss: And he says to them, "See, the man!"

en.L: And he says to them, "Look, the man!"
en.B: Pilate said to them, "Look, here is the man!"
en.R: Pilate said to them, "Look! Here is the man!"

vi.L: Và ông nói với họ: "Kìa, người ấy!"
vi.B: Phi-lát nói với họ: "Kìa, người này đây!"
vi.R: Phi-lát nói với họ: "Hãy nhìn xem! Người này đây!"

ko.L: 그리고 그가 그들에게 말한다. "보아라, 그 사람이다!"
ko.B: 빌라도가 그들에게 말했다. "보아라, 이 사람이다!"
ko.R: 빌라도가 그들에게 말했다. "봐라! 여기 이 사람이 있다!"

decisions.choice: he says: Pilate is the speaker
decisions.reason: The last person named is Jesus, but Pilate is the one who speaks to "them" in verses 4 and 6, and the words present Jesus to his accusers. The subject is left unstated in the Greek.

decisions.choice: Look, the man: Pilate presents the beaten prisoner as no threat, in pity or in scorn
decisions.reason: The words point to the man before them: beaten, in a mock crown and robe. Pilate's aim seems to be the one of verse 4, to show that this prisoner is no rival king and not worth putting to death. Whether he speaks with some pity ("see this poor man") or with contempt ("look at this fellow") the words do not say, and both may be present.

decisions.choice: the man: perhaps more than Pilate means
decisions.reason: John's reader may hear more in the words than Pilate does, as with Caiaphas in 11:49-52. The Word became flesh (1:14), and Jesus has called himself the Son of Man (1:51; 12:23, 34). Some also hear an echo of Zechariah 6:12, "Look, a man whose name is the Branch", but the wording there is not the same. John does not draw out any of these, and the deeper sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: And he says to them, "Look, the man!" (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the sentence absent (a few early witnesses)
decisions.reason: A very few early witnesses, among them the first hand of P66 and some Old Latin copies, lack this sentence. Nearly all manuscripts have it. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Look, the man (L); Look, here is the man (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Behold" is no longer everyday speech, and the Latin form of these words, "Ecce homo", is known from art rather than from speech. Literal keeps the bare Greek; Balanced and Readable add "here is" to make a natural sentence. The footnote gives the familiar "Behold the man".

decisions.choice: Pilate (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "người ấy" (L); "người này đây" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "con người" would be the closest word for "the man", but it could be confused with the title "Con Người" (Son of Man), which John does not use here.

source.text: ὅτε οὖν εἶδον αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ ὑπηρέται ἐκραύγασαν λέγοντες· Σταύρωσον σταύρωσον.

records.literal_gloss: When therefore saw him the chief priests and the officers, they cried out saying, "Crucify, crucify!"

en.L: So when the chief priests and the officers saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they shouted, saying, "Crucify, crucify!"
en.B: When the chief priests and the temple police saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they shouted, "Crucify! Crucify!"
en.R: When the leading priests and the temple guards saw Jesus, they shouted, "Crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! Crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

vi.L: Vậy khi các thầy tế lễ cả và các lính hầu thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, họ la lên rằng: "Đóng đinh! Đóng đinh!"
vi.B: Khi các thầy tế lễ cả và lính canh đền thờ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, họ la lên: "Đóng đinh! Đóng đinh!"
vi.R: Khi các thầy tế lễ cả và lính canh đền thờ thấy Đức Giê-xu, họ la lên: "Đóng đinh ông ta trên cây thập tự! Đóng đinh ông ta!"

ko.L: 그래서 대제사장들과 경비병들이 그분을 보았을 때, 소리 지르며 말했다. "십자가에 못 박으시오, 십자가에 못 박으시오!"
ko.B: 대제사장들과 성전 경비병들은 예수를 보자 소리를 질렀다. "십자가에 못 박으시오! 십자가에 못 박으시오!"
ko.R: 대제사장들과 성전 경비병들이 예수를 보고 소리쳤다. "저 사람을 십자가에 못 박으시오! 십자가에 못 박으시오!"

decisions.choice: the chief priests and the officers: the priestly leaders and the temple police who served them
alternatives: the people of Jerusalem in general
decisions.reason: The officers are the men who kept order in the temple for the chief priests; they had been sent to seize Jesus before (7:32, 45) and arrested him in the garden (18:3, 12). John names only these two groups as the ones who shout here. He says nothing of a large crowd.

decisions.choice: crucify: put to death on a cross, a Roman penalty
decisions.reason: Crucifixion was a Roman form of execution, used above all for slaves and rebels against Rome. In Judea only the Roman governor could order it (18:31). By demanding it, the chief priests ask Pilate to put Jesus to death in the Roman way, the kind of death Jesus had spoken of when he said he would be lifted up (12:32-33; 18:32).

decisions.choice: shouted: cried out loudly
decisions.reason: The verb is the one John uses for the shouts of 18:40 and 19:12, 15, and for the crowd who welcomed Jesus to Jerusalem with "Hosanna" a few days earlier (12:13).

decisions.choice: temple police (B); leading priests, temple guards (R)
decisions.reason: "Officers" alone does not say whose officers these are, so Balanced and Readable name their role (meaning decision m1), as at 7:32. Readable says "leading priests" so that "chief" is not taken as a single leader.

decisions.choice: Crucify him! Crucify him! (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has the verb alone, twice. Readable supplies "him", which the sense requires.

decisions.choice: "đóng đinh" for "crucify"; "cây thập tự" where the cross is named
decisions.reason: "đóng đinh" alone is the usual Vietnamese word for crucifixion. "cây thập tự" is the Protestant word for the cross; "thập giá" is the Catholic one (see style guide section 4).

decisions.choice: "십자가에 못 박다" for stauroo at every level
decisions.reason: The common Korean phrase for crucifixion, clear to every reader; kept for each occurrence in the trial and at the cross.

source.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Λάβετε αὐτὸν ὑμεῖς καὶ σταυρώσατε, ἐγὼ γὰρ οὐχ εὑρίσκω ἐν αὐτῷ αἰτίαν.

records.literal_gloss: Says to them the Pilate, "Take him you and crucify [him], I for not find in him a case."

en.L: Pilate says to them, "You take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and crucify [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], for I find no case in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: Pilate told them, "Take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} yourselves and crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. I find no case against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: Pilate answered, "You take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} yourselves! As for me, I find no reason to condemn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

vi.L: Phi-lát nói với họ: "Chính các ông hãy bắt người này mà đóng đinh [đi], vì tôi không tìm thấy cớ nào nơi người này."
vi.B: Phi-lát bảo họ: "Các ông tự bắt người này mà đóng đinh đi. Tôi không tìm thấy cớ nào để buộc tội ông ta."
vi.R: Phi-lát trả lời: "Các ông cứ tự đem ông ta đi mà đóng đinh! Còn tôi, tôi không tìm thấy lý do gì để kết án ông ta."

ko.L: 빌라도가 그들에게 말한다. "너희가 그를 데려가서 십자가에 못 박아라. 나는 그에게서 죄목을 찾지 못하기 때문이다."
ko.B: 빌라도가 그들에게 말했다. "너희가 직접 데려가서 십자가에 못 박아라. 나는 그에게서 아무 죄도 찾지 못하겠다."
ko.R: 빌라도가 대답했다. "그럼 너희가 데려가서 직접 십자가에 못 박아라! 나는 이 사람을 처벌할 이유를 하나도 찾지 못하겠다."

decisions.choice: take him yourselves and crucify him: a scornful retort, not a real permission
alternatives: a real handing over of Jesus to them for execution
decisions.reason: They had already told Pilate that they were not allowed to put anyone to death (18:31), and crucifixion was a Roman punishment. Pilate throws their demand back at them: if they want this, let them do it, for he will not. The verses that follow show that he did not mean it as an order or a grant of power.

decisions.choice: you ... I: both pronouns are emphatic
decisions.reason: Greek does not need the pronouns, so their presence marks a contrast: you may crucify him; I find nothing against him.

decisions.choice: case: grounds for a charge
decisions.reason: The same word as in 18:38 and 19:4 (meaning decision there). This is the third time Pilate says it.

decisions.choice: yourselves (B, R); As for me (R)
decisions.reason: English shows the emphatic "you" with "yourselves" and Readable shows the emphatic "I" with "As for me" (meaning decision m2). Readable says "answered", since Pilate is replying to their shout.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· Ἡμεῖς νόμον ἔχομεν, καὶ κατὰ τὸν νόμον ὀφείλει ἀποθανεῖν, ὅτι υἱὸν θεοῦ ἑαυτὸν ἐποίησεν.

records.literal_gloss: Answered him the Jews, "We a law have, and according to the law he ought to die, because Son of God himself he made."

en.L: The Jews answered him, "We have a law, and according to the law {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ought to die, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} [the] Son of God."
en.B: The Jewish leaders replied, "We have a law, and by that law {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must die, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} the Son of God."
en.R: The Jewish leaders answered Pilate, "We have a law, and that law says {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must die. He has made {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} out to be the Son of God."

vi.L: Người Do Thái trả lời ông: "Chúng tôi có luật pháp, và theo luật pháp ấy, người này phải chết, vì đã tự xưng mình là Con Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.B: Các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái đáp: "Chúng tôi có luật pháp, và theo luật pháp đó ông ta phải chết, vì ông ta đã tự xưng là Con Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.R: Các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái trả lời Phi-lát: "Chúng tôi có luật pháp, và luật ấy nói ông ta phải chết. Ông ta đã tự cho mình là Con Đức Chúa Trời."

ko.L: 유대인들이 그에게 대답했다. "우리에게는 율법이 있는데, 그 율법에 따르면 그는 죽어야 마땅합니다. 그가 자기 자신을 하나님의 아들로 삼았기 때문입니다."
ko.B: 유대 지도자들이 대답했다. "우리에게는 율법이 있습니다. 그 율법대로 하면 그는 죽어야 합니다. 자기가 하나님의 아들이라고 했기 때문입니다."
ko.R: 유대 지도자들이 빌라도에게 대답했다. "우리에게는 율법이 있는데, 그 율법에 따르면 저 사람은 죽어야 합니다. 저 사람이 자기를 하나님의 아들이라고 내세웠기 때문입니다."

decisions.choice: the Jews: the chief priests and their officers who have just shouted (verse 6)
decisions.reason: John has just named the speakers: the chief priests and the officers. They now answer Pilate's retort. It is not the Jewish people as a whole: Jesus and his disciples are Jews, and many in Jerusalem had welcomed him (12:12-13).

decisions.choice: we have a law: the law against blasphemy, Leviticus 24:16
decisions.reason: The law of Moses put to death anyone who blasphemed the name of the LORD (Leviticus 24:16). The charge is the one made in 5:18 and 10:33, 36: that a man claims for himself what belongs to God. Before Pilate they had so far called him only a wrongdoer (18:30); now they name a religious charge.

decisions.choice: he made himself the Son of God: their charge, which John's reader sees in a different light
decisions.reason: "Son" has no article because it comes before its verb, but it is the title: the Son of God. John's reader knows that Jesus is the Son of God (1:34, 49; 20:31). What is false in the charge is that he made himself anything: he does nothing on his own, and it is the Father who glorifies him (5:19; 8:54). Compare 5:18 and 10:33.

decisions.choice: according to the law (SBLGNT)
alternatives: according to our law (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "according to our law". The older manuscripts lack "our", and the sense is the same. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: has made himself out to be (R)
decisions.reason: Readable shows that this is a claim they reject (meaning decision m3), as at 10:33. It names Pilate, since "him" could be taken as Jesus.

decisions.choice: "người Do Thái" (L); "các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As docs/john-terms.md: Literal keeps John's word; Balanced and Readable name the authorities. The same in verses 12 and 14.

source.text: Ὅτε οὖν ἤκουσεν ὁ Πιλᾶτος τοῦτον τὸν λόγον, μᾶλλον ἐφοβήθη, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον πάλιν καὶ λέγει τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Πόθεν εἶ σύ;

records.literal_gloss: When therefore heard the Pilate this the word, more he was afraid, \v 9 and he went into the praetorium again and says to the Jesus, "From where are you?"

en.L: So when Pilate heard this word, he was more afraid, \v 9 and he went into the praetorium again and says to Jesus, "Where are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} from?"
en.B: When Pilate heard this, he was even more afraid. \v 9 He went back inside the headquarters and said to Jesus, "Where do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come from?"
en.R: When Pilate heard this, he was even more afraid. \v 9 He went back into the palace and asked Jesus, "Where do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come from?"

vi.L: Vậy khi Phi-lát nghe lời này, ông càng sợ hơn, \v 9 và ông lại vào dinh tổng đốc và nói với Đức Giê-xu: "Anh từ đâu đến?"
vi.B: Khi Phi-lát nghe lời ấy, ông càng sợ hơn nữa. \v 9 Ông trở vào trong dinh tổng đốc và hỏi Đức Giê-xu: "Anh từ đâu đến?"
vi.R: Nghe vậy, Phi-lát càng sợ hơn. \v 9 Ông trở vào dinh và hỏi Đức Giê-xu: "Anh từ đâu đến?"

ko.L: 그래서 빌라도는 이 말을 듣고 더욱 두려워하여, \v 9 다시 관정 안으로 들어가서 예수께 말한다. "너는 어디에서 왔느냐?"
ko.B: 빌라도는 이 말을 듣고 더욱 두려워졌다. \v 9 그는 다시 총독 관저 안으로 들어가서 예수께 물었다. "너는 어디에서 왔느냐?"
ko.R: 빌라도는 이 말을 듣고 더욱 겁이 났다. \v 9 그래서 다시 관저 안으로 들어가 예수께 물었다. "너는 어디에서 온 사람이냐?"

decisions.choice: even more afraid: Pilate was already uneasy, and now his fear grows
decisions.reason: John has not said that Pilate was afraid before, but the comparative fits his efforts to be rid of the case (18:38-39; 19:4, 6). The word can also mean simply "very afraid"; the sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: this word: the claim that Jesus made himself the Son of God
alternatives: fear only of a riot or of being reported to Rome
decisions.reason: John does not say why this frightened Pilate. Romans told stories of sons of gods and of divine men, and a Roman could fear having harmed one; Pilate may also have feared trouble from the accusers. His next question, about where Jesus comes from, suggests the first.

decisions.choice: the praetorium: the Roman governor's headquarters in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The word was used for a Roman governor's official residence. Jesus has been held inside (18:28, 33), while his accusers stayed outside.

decisions.choice: Where are you from: Pilate asks about more than a home town
alternatives: a question about which region he came from
decisions.reason: Where Jesus comes from is a question that runs through the Gospel (7:27-29; 8:14; 9:29-30). He has already told Pilate that his kingdom is not from this world (18:36). The reader knows the answer: he came from the Father, from above (3:31; 16:28).

decisions.choice: the headquarters (B); the palace (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the praetorium was (meaning decision m3), as in 18:28 and 18:33; Literal keeps the Roman word.

decisions.choice: Pilate to Jesus: "anh", himself "tôi" (19:8-11)
decisions.reason: As in 18:33: a governor to a prisoner, neither archaic nor deferential. "anh" is Pilate's word and takes no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: Pilate speaks to Jesus in the plain style (해라체: "너는 ... 왔느냐?"), as in 18:33-38
decisions.reason: The judge keeps the form he used with the prisoner in chapter 18; his growing fear shows in the narrative, not in a change of speech level. A reviewer may prefer 하오체.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀπόκρισιν οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: But the Jesus an answer not gave him.

en.L: But Jesus did not give him an answer.
en.B: But Jesus gave him no answer.
en.R: But Jesus did not answer him.

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu không cho ông một lời đáp nào.
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu không đáp lại ông.
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu không trả lời ông.

ko.L: 그러나 예수께서는 그에게 대답을 주지 않으셨다.
ko.B: 그러나 예수께서는 그에게 아무 대답도 하지 않으셨다.
ko.R: 그러나 예수께서는 빌라도에게 대답하지 않으셨다.

decisions.choice: Jesus gave no answer: perhaps an echo of Isaiah 53:7
decisions.reason: The servant of the LORD in Isaiah 53:7 is like a lamb led to the slaughter that does not open its mouth. Mark 14:61 and 15:5 also tell of Jesus keeping silent before his judges. John does not quote Isaiah here, so the echo is possible but not certain.

decisions.choice: his silence: he has already given Pilate his answer
decisions.reason: Jesus has told Pilate that his kingdom is not from this world and that he came to bear witness to the truth (18:36-37), and Pilate turned away from it (18:38). John does not explain the silence, but it follows that refusal.

decisions.choice: did not give him an answer (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the noun "answer" with "give", as the Greek has it; Balanced and Readable use natural forms of the same idea.

source.text: λέγει οὖν αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Ἐμοὶ οὐ λαλεῖς;

records.literal_gloss: Says therefore to him the Pilate, "To me not you speak?"

en.L: So Pilate says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "To me {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not speak?"
en.B: So Pilate said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} refusing to speak to me?"
en.R: So Pilate said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not even talk to me?"

vi.L: Vậy Phi-lát nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Với tôi, anh không nói sao?"
vi.B: Vậy Phi-lát nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Anh không chịu nói với tôi sao?"
vi.R: Vậy Phi-lát nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ngay cả với tôi mà anh cũng không chịu nói à?"

ko.L: 그래서 빌라도가 그분께 말한다. "나에게 말하지 않느냐?"
ko.B: 그래서 빌라도가 예수께 말했다. "나에게 말을 하지 않겠다는 것이냐?"
ko.R: 그래서 빌라도가 예수께 말했다. "나에게 한마디도 하지 않을 셈이냐?"

decisions.choice: to me: placed first for emphasis, to me, the governor
decisions.reason: The pronoun stands first in the question. Pilate is struck that a prisoner whose life he controls will not answer him, of all people; the next sentence says why.

decisions.choice: Are you refusing to speak to me (B); Will you not even talk to me (R)
alternatives: You do not speak to me?
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show the emphasis on "me" by the form of the question (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps the Greek word order.

source.text: οὐκ οἶδας ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχω ἀπολῦσαί σε καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔχω σταυρῶσαί σε;

records.literal_gloss: Not know you that authority I have to release you and authority I have to crucify you?

en.L: Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not know that I have authority to release {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and I have authority to crucify {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?
en.B: Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not know that I have authority to set {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} free and authority to crucify {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?
en.R: Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not understand that I have the power to let {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} go? I also have the power to have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} crucified!

vi.L: Anh không biết rằng tôi có quyền tha anh và có quyền đóng đinh anh sao?
vi.B: Anh không biết rằng tôi có quyền thả anh và cũng có quyền đóng đinh anh sao?
vi.R: Anh không hiểu rằng tôi có quyền thả anh đi sao? Tôi cũng có quyền ra lệnh đóng đinh anh!

ko.L: 내가 너를 놓아줄 권한도 있고 너를 십자가에 못 박을 권한도 있다는 것을 알지 못하느냐?
ko.B: 나에게는 너를 풀어 줄 권한도 있고 십자가에 못 박을 권한도 있다는 것을 모르느냐?
ko.R: 나에게 너를 풀어 줄 권한이 있다는 것을 모르느냐? 너를 십자가에 못 박게 할 권한도 있다!

decisions.choice: authority: the legal right and power to decide
decisions.reason: The word means the right to act, and the power that goes with it. As the Roman governor of Judea, Pilate held the power of life and death over a prisoner like Jesus (18:31). John uses the same word for the authority the Father gave the Son (5:27; 10:18; 17:2), and Jesus takes it up in his reply.

decisions.choice: release ... crucify (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts put the two the other way round: "to crucify you, and ... to release you". The older manuscripts have the order given here. The sense is the same. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Do you not know: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The negative form expects agreement: surely you know this. Pilate means it as a warning.

decisions.choice: power (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "power", the everyday word, here and in verse 11, so that Jesus's reply is heard as an answer to Pilate's claim. Literal and Balanced keep "authority" (meaning decision m1). Readable says "have you crucified", since the governor's soldiers would carry it out.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐκ εἶχες ἐξουσίαν κατ’ ἐμοῦ οὐδεμίαν εἰ μὴ ἦν δεδομένον σοι ἄνωθεν· διὰ τοῦτο ὁ παραδούς μέ σοι μείζονα ἁμαρτίαν ἔχει.

records.literal_gloss: Answered him Jesus, "Not you would have authority against me none, if not it was given to you from above; because of this the [one] having handed over me to you greater sin has."

en.L: Jesus answered him, "You would have no authority over {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} at all if it had not been given to you from above; because of this the one who handed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over to you has [the] greater sin."
en.B: Jesus answered, "You would have no authority over {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} at all unless it had been given to you from above. That is why the one who handed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over to you carries the greater sin."
en.R: Jesus answered, "You would not have any power over {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} if God had not given it to you. So the person who handed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over to you is even more guilty of sin than you are."

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu trả lời ông: "Ông sẽ không có quyền gì trên {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cả, nếu quyền ấy không được ban cho ông từ trên cao; vì vậy kẻ đã nộp {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho ông mắc tội lớn hơn."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Ông chẳng có quyền gì trên {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cả, nếu không phải từ trên cao ban cho ông. Vì thế, kẻ đã nộp {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho ông mang tội nặng hơn."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Ông sẽ không có chút quyền gì trên {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nếu Đức Chúa Trời không ban cho ông. Vì vậy, người đã nộp {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho ông còn có tội nặng hơn ông."

ko.L: 예수께서 그에게 대답하셨다. "위에서 너에게 주어지지 않았다면, 너는 나를 거스를 아무 권한도 없었을 것이다. 이 때문에 나를 너에게 넘겨준 사람에게 더 큰 죄가 있다."
ko.B: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "위에서 너에게 주어진 것이 아니라면, 너는 나에 대하여 아무 권한도 없었을 것이다. 그러므로 나를 너에게 넘겨준 사람의 죄가 더 크다."
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "하나님께서 너에게 주지 않으셨다면, 너는 나에게 아무 권한도 없었을 것이다. 그러니 나를 너에게 넘겨준 사람은 너보다 더 큰 죄를 지은 것이다."

decisions.choice: from above: from God
decisions.reason: John uses this word for what comes from God and from heaven (3:3, 31); compare 3:27, "unless it has been given him from heaven". Pilate's power over Jesus comes from God, not finally from the emperor, and it is given only for this hour.

decisions.choice: it had been given: the whole matter, not only the word "authority"
alternatives: the authority itself had been given
decisions.reason: The participle is neuter, while the word for authority is feminine. So "it" most likely means the whole situation, Pilate's power over Jesus at this moment, which God has allowed. The sense is the same as if authority alone were meant.

decisions.choice: because of this ... the greater sin: Pilate is guilty, but the one who handed Jesus over is more guilty
alternatives: Pilate has no sin at all
decisions.reason: Pilate acts with a power that God has given to his office, though he is still responsible for how he uses it; "greater" means that Pilate's sin is real too. The one who handed Jesus over did so knowingly, from his own will, and set the whole matter in motion. Jesus speaks of guilt in this one case, not of any group or people.

decisions.choice: the one who handed me over to you: most likely Caiaphas, the high priest
alternatives: the chief priests as a group
decisions.reason: The word is singular. Caiaphas sent Jesus to Pilate (18:24, 28) and had said that one man should die for the nation (11:49-50; 18:14), and Pilate has said, "Your nation and the chief priests handed you over to me" (18:35). Others take it to mean Judas, whom John often calls the one who handed Jesus over (6:64, 71; 13:11; 18:2, 5); but Judas handed him over to the men sent by the chief priests (18:3), not to Pilate. Either way it names a single person who acted, not a people.

decisions.choice: if God had not given it to you (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who is meant by "from above" (meaning decision m1) and uses "power" as in verse 10.

decisions.choice: carries the greater sin (B); is even more guilty of sin than you are (R)
decisions.reason: To "have sin" is a way of speaking of guilt, as in 9:41 and 15:22, 24. Readable says "even more ... than you are" to show that Pilate's own guilt is real (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Jesus to Pilate: "ông", himself "Ta"
decisions.reason: As in 18:34: courteous to the official, without deference.

source.text: ἐκ τούτου ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐζήτει ἀπολῦσαι αὐτόν· οἱ δὲ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐκραύγασαν λέγοντες· Ἐὰν τοῦτον ἀπολύσῃς, οὐκ εἶ φίλος τοῦ Καίσαρος· πᾶς ὁ βασιλέα ἑαυτὸν ποιῶν ἀντιλέγει τῷ Καίσαρι.

records.literal_gloss: From this the Pilate was seeking to release him; but the Jews cried out saying, "If this [man] you release, not you are friend of the Caesar; everyone the king himself making speaks against the Caesar."

en.L: From this [time] Pilate was seeking to release {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but the Jews shouted, saying, "If you release this [man], you are not a friend of Caesar; everyone who makes himself a king speaks against Caesar."
en.B: From then on Pilate tried to set {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} free, but the Jewish leaders shouted, "If you let this man go, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who claims to be a king is setting himself against Caesar."
en.R: After this, Pilate kept trying to find a way to let Jesus go. But the Jewish leaders shouted, "If you let this man go, you are not Caesar's friend! Anyone who says he is a king is an enemy of Caesar, the emperor!"

vi.L: Từ [lúc] đó, Phi-lát tìm cách tha {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhưng người Do Thái la lên rằng: "Nếu quan tha người này, quan không phải là bạn của Sê-sa. Ai tự xưng mình là vua thì chống lại Sê-sa."
vi.B: Từ lúc đó, Phi-lát tìm cách thả {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhưng các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái la lên: "Nếu quan thả người này, quan không phải là bạn của Sê-sa. Ai tự xưng là vua tức là chống lại Sê-sa."
vi.R: Từ đó, Phi-lát cứ tìm cách thả Đức Giê-xu. Nhưng các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái la lên: "Nếu quan thả người này thì quan không phải là bạn của Sê-sa! Ai tự xưng là vua đều là kẻ thù của Sê-sa, tức là hoàng đế!"

ko.L: 이때부터 빌라도는 그분을 놓아주려고 애썼다. 그러나 유대인들이 소리 지르며 말했다. "이 [사람]을 놓아주시면 [총독님은] 가이사의 친구가 아닙니다. 자기를 왕으로 삼는 사람은 누구나 가이사를 거슬러 말하는 것입니다."
ko.B: 이때부터 빌라도는 예수를 놓아주려고 애썼다. 그러나 유대 지도자들이 소리를 질렀다. "이 사람을 놓아주시면 총독님은 가이사의 친구가 아닙니다. 자기를 왕이라고 하는 사람은 누구나 가이사에게 맞서는 것입니다."
ko.R: 그 뒤로 빌라도는 예수를 풀어 줄 방법을 계속 찾았다. 그러나 유대 지도자들이 소리쳤다. "이 사람을 놓아주시면 총독님은 황제의 친구가 아닙니다! 자기가 왕이라고 하는 사람은 누구나 로마 황제 가이사의 원수입니다!"

decisions.choice: from this: from then on, and because of what Jesus had said
decisions.reason: The phrase can mark time ("from then on") or a reason ("because of this"); John uses it the same way in 6:66, where both senses are possible. Here Jesus's answer is the turning point, so both fit.

decisions.choice: was seeking: kept trying
decisions.reason: The imperfect shows repeated or continued attempts. Pilate kept looking for a way to release Jesus, without success.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the chief priests and their officers, with those who stood with them outside the praetorium
decisions.reason: They are the accusers of verses 6-7, who answer Pilate again; in verse 15 John names the chief priests as the ones who speak for them. Others may have stood with them, as the shout for Barabbas suggests (18:39-40), but John does not describe a crowd. It is not the Jewish people as a whole: Jesus and his disciples are Jews.

decisions.choice: Caesar's friend: loyal to the emperor, perhaps also an honored title
decisions.reason: "Caesar" here means the Roman emperor, Tiberius at this time (Luke 3:1). "Friend of Caesar" means one loyal to him; it was also used of men honored with the emperor's favor, but whether Pilate held such a title is not known. The threat is plain: if he releases a man accused of claiming to be king, they will report him as disloyal.

decisions.choice: makes himself a king speaks against Caesar: claims to be a king and so opposes the emperor
decisions.reason: The verb means to speak against and so to oppose; to set oneself up as a king in a Roman province was rebellion. "Makes himself a king" repeats the form of the charge in verse 7, "made himself the Son of God": the accusers now turn the religious charge into a political one.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: Caesar, the emperor (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says who Caesar was, the first time the name comes in the passage (meaning decision m4), and says "enemy of" for "speaks against" (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: the accusers to Pilate: "quan"
decisions.reason: As in 18:30: "quan" is how subjects address an official; "ngài" is kept for the deity pronoun.

decisions.choice: the accusers' argument in 합쇼체, with "[총독님은]" (L) / "총독님은" (B, R) for "you"
decisions.reason: As in 18:30: Korean does not call a superior "you", and the threat is put as an argument, not a shout, so it keeps the polite level.

source.text: Ὁ οὖν Πιλᾶτος ἀκούσας τῶν λόγων τούτων ἤγαγεν ἔξω τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐπὶ βήματος εἰς τόπον λεγόμενον Λιθόστρωτον, Ἑβραϊστὶ δὲ Γαββαθα.

records.literal_gloss: The therefore Pilate, having heard the words these, brought outside the Jesus and sat on [the] judgment seat at a place called Stone Pavement, in Hebrew but Gabbatha.

en.L: So Pilate, having heard these words, brought Jesus outside and sat down on [the] judgment seat at a place called [the] Stone Pavement, but in Hebrew Gabbatha.
en.B: When Pilate heard this, he brought Jesus outside and took his seat on the judgment seat at the place known as the Stone Pavement, in Hebrew Gabbatha.
en.R: When Pilate heard this, he brought Jesus outside. He sat down on the judge's seat at a place called the Stone Pavement. In Hebrew its name was Gabbatha.

vi.L: Vậy Phi-lát, nghe những lời này, dẫn Đức Giê-xu ra ngoài và ngồi trên ghế xử án tại nơi gọi là Nền Lát Đá, còn tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ là Ga-ba-tha.
vi.B: Khi nghe những lời ấy, Phi-lát dẫn Đức Giê-xu ra ngoài và ngồi lên ghế xử án, tại nơi gọi là Nền Lát Đá, tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ là Ga-ba-tha.
vi.R: Nghe vậy, Phi-lát dẫn Đức Giê-xu ra ngoài. Ông ngồi trên ghế quan tòa tại một nơi gọi là Nền Lát Đá. Trong tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ, nơi ấy gọi là Ga-ba-tha.

ko.L: 그래서 빌라도는 이 말들을 듣고 예수를 밖으로 데리고 나가서, 돌을 깐 뜰, 히브리 말로는 가바다라고 하는 곳에서 재판석에 앉았다.
ko.B: 빌라도는 이 말을 듣고 예수를 밖으로 데리고 나왔다. 그리고 돌을 깐 뜰이라는 곳, 히브리 말로 가바다라는 곳에서 재판석에 앉았다.
ko.R: 빌라도는 이 말을 듣고 예수를 밖으로 데리고 나왔다. 그리고 돌을 깔아 놓은 뜰이라는 곳에서 재판관 자리에 앉았다. 그곳은 히브리 말로 가바다라고 했다.

decisions.choice: sat down: Pilate took his seat
alternatives: Pilate seated Jesus on the judgment seat
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "sat" in John (12:14), and a governor sat on the judgment seat to give sentence (Matthew 27:19; Acts 25:6, 17). The verb can also mean "seated someone", and the sentence could then mean that Pilate set Jesus on the judgment seat in mockery, as the soldiers had dressed him as a king. That would fit John's irony, but without an object stated the plain sense is more likely.

decisions.choice: judgment seat: the raised platform where a Roman official sat to give his decision
decisions.reason: The word means a platform reached by steps. A Roman magistrate gave judgment from it in public (Acts 18:12; 25:6). By sitting there Pilate makes his decision formal.

decisions.choice: the Stone Pavement, in Hebrew Gabbatha: two names for the same place
decisions.reason: The first name means a floor laid with stones. "In Hebrew" means the language of the Jews of the land, which in daily speech was mostly Aramaic (as at 5:2). Gabbatha is not a translation of the first name; its meaning is uncertain, perhaps "height" or "raised place". The exact place in Jerusalem is not known.

decisions.choice: these words: the threat of verse 12
decisions.reason: It is the warning that he would be no friend of Caesar that moves Pilate to act.

decisions.choice: in Hebrew
decisions.reason: Keeps the word John used, as at 5:2; meaning decision m3 explains which language this was.

decisions.choice: the judge's seat (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the seat was for (meaning decision m2) and breaks the long sentence.

decisions.choice: "Nền Lát Đá"; "tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ"
decisions.reason: The place name is translated as a name, capitalised. "tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ" follows John's word and the Protestant spelling; the language spoken was probably Aramaic, as the English notes say.

decisions.choice: "돌을 깐 뜰" (L, B); "돌을 깔아 놓은 뜰" (R); "히브리 말" for Hebraisti
decisions.reason: The Greek name describes a stone-paved court; the older Sino-Korean term "박석" is unfamiliar today. "히브리 말" follows John's own word; what language he means is left to a note, as in English.

source.text: ἦν δὲ παρασκευὴ τοῦ πάσχα, ὥρα ἦν ὡς ἕκτη.

records.literal_gloss: It was now Preparation of the Passover; hour was about sixth.

en.L: Now it was [the] Preparation of the Passover; it was about the sixth hour.
en.B: It was the day of Preparation of the Passover, about noon.
en.R: It was the day of Preparation, when people got ready for the Passover. The time was about noon.

vi.L: Bấy giờ là [ngày] Chuẩn Bị của Lễ Vượt Qua; khoảng giờ thứ sáu.
vi.B: Hôm ấy là ngày Chuẩn Bị cho Lễ Vượt Qua, vào khoảng giữa trưa.
vi.R: Hôm ấy là ngày Chuẩn Bị, khi mọi người sửa soạn cho Lễ Vượt Qua. Lúc đó khoảng mười hai giờ trưa.

ko.L: 그날은 유월절 준비일이었고, 때는 여섯째 시쯤이었다.
ko.B: 그날은 유월절 준비일이었고, 시간은 낮 열두 시쯤이었다.
ko.R: 그날은 유월절을 준비하는 날이었다. 시간은 낮 열두 시쯤이었다.

decisions.choice: the Preparation of the Passover: the day before the Passover, when the meal was made ready
alternatives: the Friday of the Passover week
decisions.reason: On the day of preparation the Passover lambs were killed in the afternoon (Exodus 12:6) and the meal was eaten that evening, when the feast began. This fits 18:28, where the accusers have not yet eaten the Passover. The same word was also the name for Friday, the day of preparation before the Sabbath (19:31, 42; Mark 15:42), and some read it here as "the Friday of Passover week". Mark 14:12-16 presents the last supper as a Passover meal, so the two accounts need to be read together; the footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: about the sixth hour: about noon
alternatives: about six in the morning, counting from midnight
decisions.reason: Hours were counted from sunrise, about six in the morning (see the notes at 1:39 and 4:6), so the sixth hour was about midday. Mark 15:25 says Jesus was crucified at the third hour, about nine in the morning. Times of day were usually given loosely ("about"). Counting from midnight, which some have proposed for John, would give six in the morning. The difference is noted here, not settled.

decisions.choice: noon on the day of preparation: perhaps a link with the Passover lambs
alternatives: the time is given only as a fact
decisions.reason: At about this hour the preparations for killing the Passover lambs were beginning. John has called Jesus the Lamb of God (1:29, 36), and he will connect the Passover lamb with Jesus's death (19:36; Exodus 12:46). He does not draw the link here, so it is possible rather than certain.

decisions.choice: about the sixth hour (Literal); about noon (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for clock times in John: Literal keeps the hour as counted then, Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: the day of Preparation (B, R); when people got ready for the Passover (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "day". Readable says what the day was for (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "ngày Chuẩn Bị", capitalised as the name of a day
decisions.reason: "ngày sắm sửa" is the old Protestant wording; "ngày Chuẩn Bị" is current Vietnamese for the same thing and reads as the day's name. Used again in 19:31 and 19:42.

decisions.choice: "여섯째 시쯤" (L); "낮 열두 시쯤" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Clock time as the style guide sets it (section 5): Literal keeps the Greek count, Balanced and Readable give the modern time.

source.text: καὶ λέγει τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις· Ἴδε ὁ βασιλεὺς ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And he says to the Jews, "See, the king of you!"

en.L: And he says to the Jews, "Look, your King!"
en.B: Pilate said to the Jewish leaders, "Look, here is your King!"
en.R: Pilate said to the Jewish leaders, "Look! Here is your King!"

vi.L: Và ông nói với người Do Thái: "Kìa, Vua của các ông!"
vi.B: Phi-lát nói với các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái: "Kìa, Vua của các ông đây!"
vi.R: Phi-lát nói với các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái: "Hãy nhìn xem! Vua của các ông đây!"

ko.L: 그리고 그가 유대인들에게 말한다. "보아라, 너희의 왕이다!"
ko.B: 빌라도가 유대 지도자들에게 말했다. "보아라, 너희 왕이다!"
ko.R: 빌라도가 유대 지도자들에게 말했다. "봐라! 여기 너희 왕이 있다!"

decisions.choice: the Jews: the chief priests and their officers, with those who stood with them before the judgment seat
decisions.reason: Pilate speaks to the accusers of verses 6-12; in verse 15 John names the chief priests as the ones who answer. It is not the Jewish people as a whole. Yet Pilate addresses them as speaking for the nation, whose king he says Jesus is.

decisions.choice: Look, your King: Pilate's taunt, which John's reader knows to be true
decisions.reason: The words match verse 5, "Look, the man". Pilate mocks both the prisoner and those who accused him of claiming to be king. John's reader knows that Jesus is the King of Israel (1:49; 12:13-15) and that his kingdom is not from this world (18:36).

decisions.choice: he says: Pilate, seated on the judgment seat
decisions.reason: The subject is Pilate, who has just taken his seat (verse 13).

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: Pilate; here is (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker and say "here is", as in verse 5, so the two sayings are heard together.

source.text: ἐκραύγασαν οὖν ἐκεῖνοι· Ἆρον ἆρον, σταύρωσον αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Cried out therefore those, "Take away, take away, crucify him!"

en.L: So those [men] shouted, "Take [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] away, take [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] away, crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.B: They shouted back, "Away with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! Away with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! Crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.R: But they shouted, "Take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away! Take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away! Crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

vi.L: Vậy những người ấy la lên: "Đem [ông ta] đi, đem [ông ta] đi, đóng đinh ông ta!"
vi.B: Họ la lên: "Trừ khử ông ta đi! Trừ khử ông ta đi! Đóng đinh ông ta!"
vi.R: Nhưng họ la lên: "Đem ông ta đi! Đem ông ta đi! Đóng đinh ông ta!"

ko.L: 그러자 그 사람들이 소리 질렀다. "치우시오, 치우시오, 그를 십자가에 못 박으시오!"
ko.B: 그들이 다시 소리쳤다. "없애 버리시오! 없애 버리시오! 십자가에 못 박으시오!"
ko.R: 그러나 그들은 소리쳤다. "저 사람을 없애 버리시오! 없애 버리시오! 십자가에 못 박으시오!"

decisions.choice: take away: remove him, that is, put him to death
alternatives: take him out of our sight
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift up and carry off. Shouted at a prisoner, it demands his removal by death, as in Luke 23:18 and Acts 22:22. The cry is doubled, as "Crucify, crucify" was in verse 6.

decisions.choice: those men: the ones Pilate has just addressed
decisions.reason: The pronoun points back to those of verse 14, and the next sentence names the chief priests as their spokesmen.

decisions.choice: Take [him] away (L); Away with him (B)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "him", which the Greek leaves unstated; Balanced uses the English idiom for demanding someone's removal. Readable says "Take him away".

source.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Τὸν βασιλέα ὑμῶν σταυρώσω;

records.literal_gloss: Says to them the Pilate, "The king of you shall I crucify?"

en.L: Pilate says to them, "Shall I crucify your King?"
en.B: Pilate said to them, "Shall I crucify your King?"
en.R: Pilate asked them, "Do you want me to crucify your King?"

vi.L: Phi-lát nói với họ: "Vua của các ông, tôi phải đóng đinh sao?"
vi.B: Phi-lát hỏi họ: "Tôi phải đóng đinh Vua của các ông sao?"
vi.R: Phi-lát hỏi họ: "Các ông muốn tôi đóng đinh Vua của các ông à?"

ko.L: 빌라도가 그들에게 말한다. "너희의 왕을 내가 십자가에 못 박으랴?"
ko.B: 빌라도가 그들에게 말했다. "너희 왕을 내가 십자가에 못 박아야 하겠느냐?"
ko.R: 빌라도가 그들에게 물었다. "너희는 내가 너희 왕을 십자가에 못 박기를 바라느냐?"

decisions.choice: your King: placed first for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Greek begins with "your King": is it your own king that I am to crucify? The verb asks what he should do.

decisions.choice: your King: Pilate presses the taunt of verse 14
decisions.reason: Pilate holds them to the title. Whether he is mocking them or making one more attempt to release Jesus, he forces them to say what they will say next.

decisions.choice: Do you want me to crucify (R)
decisions.reason: Readable puts the question in a form young readers use. The emphasis on "your" is left to the voice.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς· Οὐκ ἔχομεν βασιλέα εἰ μὴ Καίσαρα.

records.literal_gloss: Answered the chief priests, "Not we have king except Caesar."

en.L: The chief priests answered, "We have no king except Caesar."
en.B: The chief priests replied, "We have no king but Caesar."
en.R: The leading priests answered, "The only king we have is Caesar!"

vi.L: Các thầy tế lễ cả trả lời: "Chúng tôi không có vua nào ngoài Sê-sa."
vi.B: Các thầy tế lễ cả đáp: "Chúng tôi chẳng có vua nào khác ngoài Sê-sa."
vi.R: Các thầy tế lễ cả trả lời: "Vua duy nhất của chúng tôi là Sê-sa!"

ko.L: 대제사장들이 대답했다. "우리에게는 가이사 외에는 왕이 없습니다."
ko.B: 대제사장들이 대답했다. "우리에게는 가이사 말고는 왕이 없습니다."
ko.R: 대제사장들이 대답했다. "우리 왕은 가이사 황제뿐입니다!"

decisions.choice: the chief priests: John names these speakers
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: Here John says who answered: the chief priests. The words are theirs, spoken as leaders before the governor; John does not put them in the mouth of the people.

decisions.choice: we have no king but Caesar: the irony of the chief priests' words
alternatives: a simple statement of political fact
decisions.reason: In Israel's Scriptures God himself is the King of his people (Judges 8:23; 1 Samuel 8:7; Isaiah 33:22), and Israel hoped for the Messiah, the King of Israel (1:49; 12:13). To press Pilate to act, the chief priests, who served God in his temple, say that they have no king but the emperor. John records the words without comment; the reader feels their weight.

decisions.choice: Caesar: the Roman emperor
decisions.reason: As in verse 12. In this period the high priest held office under Roman rule and was appointed by the Roman governor; the chief priests' position depended on Rome.

decisions.choice: The only king we have is Caesar (R); leading priests (R)
alternatives: We have no king but Caesar (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Readable puts the exception in a plain positive form; "leading priests" as in verse 6.

ko.B: 그러자 빌라도는 예수를 십자가에 못 박도록 그들에게 넘겨주었다.

decisions.choice: to them: to the will of the chief priests, while Roman soldiers carried out the sentence
alternatives: handed him to the chief priests, who carried out the crucifixion
decisions.reason: By the grammar, "them" are the last people named, the chief priests (verse 15). Yet the crucifixion was carried out by Roman soldiers (19:23, 32), on the governor's order, and the charge set over the cross was Pilate's (19:19). So the sense is that Pilate gave Jesus up to what they demanded and handed him over for execution; it does not mean the chief priests crucified him themselves. Compare Luke 23:25, "he delivered Jesus over to their will". Every level keeps "to them" as the Greek has it.

decisions.choice: handed over: the same verb used all through the story
decisions.reason: Judas handed Jesus over (18:2, 5), the chief priests handed him over to Pilate (18:30, 35), and Jesus has spoken of the one who handed him over (19:11). Now Pilate, who has said three times that he finds no case against him, hands him over to be crucified. The responsibility for the sentence is the Roman governor's.

decisions.choice: Pilate (B, R); Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Pilate, since the last speakers were the chief priests. Readable names Jesus. "To them" stays at every level (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: they: those to whom Jesus was handed over; in fact the soldiers carried out the crucifixion
decisions.reason: John does not name the subject. It follows on from "them" in the sentence before, but the ones who crucified Jesus were the soldiers (19:23). This sentence opens the account of the crucifixion that follows.

decisions.choice: took: received him into their charge
decisions.reason: The verb means to take or receive someone from another. It is the word used in 1:11, "his own did not receive him"; whether John means the reader to hear that echo is uncertain.

decisions.choice: So they took Jesus (SBLGNT)
alternatives: They took Jesus and led him away (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and led him away", and some have other short additions. The older manuscripts have the shorter text; the sense is the same. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: took charge of (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that Jesus was received into custody (meaning decision m2).
